CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.P.SANDESH  and  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VENKATESH NAIK T  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.P.SANDESH) Heard the learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the appellant/State and the learned counsel for respondent No.1.
2.

This appeal is filed by the State against the acquittal of the accused for the offences punishable under Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act ('POCSO Act' for short),
Section 376 of IPC read with NC: 2026:KHC:5764-DB HC-KAR Section 4 of POCSO Act and also Sections 8 and 18 of POCSO Act read with Section 511 of IPC.

sentences.text: The factual matrix of the case of the prosecution is that one month prior to 05.10.2015 while the minor girl P.W.1 was going to school by walk, the accused has followed her, dragged her by holding her hands and teased and also made gestures towards her.

On 20.09.2015 at about 1.00 p.m., at the cattle shed of Amrutheshwarahalli belonging to C.W.2 Eregowda, the accused has subjected her for sexual act, who is a minor and thereafter, has put her and her family members in fear of death.

It is also the case of the prosecution that when P.W.1 was going to school by walk, the accused has wrongfully restrained her, teased, unrobbed and attempted to rape on her and thereby, committed an offence under Sections 8 and 18 of POCSO Act read with Section 511 of IPC.
The prosecution in order to prove the case, examined P.W.1 to P.W.12 and also relied upon the documents at Exs.P.1 to 14(a) and got marked M.O.1 to M.O.15.
Ex.D.1 portion in the statement of P.W.1 are marked by the defence.
NC: 2026:KHC:5764-DB HC-KAR 4.

The Trial Court considered the evidence of P.W.1 victim girl, P.W.2 father of the victim girl, P.W.3 owner of cattle shed, P.W.4 brother of the victim girl, P.W.5 friend of the victim girl, P.W.6 doctor,
who subjected the victim girl for medical examination, P.W.7 and P.W.8 witnesses to the spot mahazar, P.W.9 teacher, P.W.10 WPC, who recorded the statement of victim girl, P.W.11 and P.W.12 Investigating Officers and acquitted the accused.
5. Being aggrieved by the order of acquittal, the present appeal is filed by the State.

6. The learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the appellant/State would vehemently contend that the Trial Court failed to properly appreciate the material evidence adducted by the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused.
Non -appreciation of evidence and material on record in the proper perspective has resulted in miscarriage of justice.
The evidence of P.W.1 victim girl is sufficient to bring home the guilt of the accused.
She has corroborated the averments made in the complaint, which is marked as Ex.P.1.

The learned counsel contend that the Trial Court has not NC: 2026:KHC:5764-DB HC-KAR appreciated both oral and documentary evidence placed on record in its proper perspective and hence, it requires interference of this Court to set aside the order of the Trial Court.
7.
Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.1/accused would vehemently contend that the Trial Court has rightly appreciated both oral and documentary evidence placed on record.
The learned counsel contend that the evidence of P.W.1 victim girl is not consistent and trustworthy.
The evidence of P.W.1 is not supported by the medical evidence and hence, the Trial Court acquitted the accused.

8. Having heard the learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the appellant/State and the learned counsel for respondent No.1/accused, the points that arise for the consideration of this Court are:
(i) Whether the Trial Court committed an error in acquitting the accused for the offences which were invoked against the accused and whether it requires interference The State Of Karnataka vs Dinesha @ Dini @ Dayananda on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130155103/
3 of this Court?
 (ii) What order?
 NC: 2026:KHC:5764-DB HC-KAR Point No.(i):
9.

sentences.text: It is the case of the prosecution that the victim girl was aged about 15 years as per the documents at Exs.P.8 and 9.
The Trial Court has taken note of that the accused and P.W.1 are residents of the same village and no dispute with regard to the said fact.
But P.W.1 used to go to Kandegala everyday for school by bicycle and this fact is also not in dispute.

Whether the incident as alleged by the prosecution on 05.10.2015 has taken place, is to be considered and considering the evidence of P.W.1, she fails to say the exact day and date of alleged incident before the Court.
Besides, she deposes that on that particular day itself, accused had put threat to her life and this is an omission on the part of P.W.1 with regard to the case of the prosecution.
There is no corroborative evidence available for the prosecution.
Further, she has deposed that on 20.10.2015 at about 1.00 p.m. when she had come to backyard to attend nature call, she was subjected to rape by the accused at the cattle shed of P.W.3.
She might have confused the date of alleged incident, since the date of incident was on 20.09.2015 as per the case of the prosecution.

According to her, on 03.11.2015, on her way to NC:
2026:KHC:5764-DB HC-KAR the school, the accused had attempted to commit rape on her.
But in order to prove the case of the prosecution, the very evidence of P.W.1 is not consistent and not trustworthy.
There are material omissions in the case of the prosecution.
10. It is pertinent to note that though the father of the victim girl P.W.2 has been examined and P.W.4 supports the case of prosecution, they are hearsay witnesses.
Their evidence is based on the information given to them by the victim girl.
But the victim girl's evidence is also not supported by medical evidence.
The same is taken note of by the Trial Court in paragraph No.18.

The evidence of the doctor is very clear that she has subjected P.W.1 for medical examination and given the report in terms of Ex.P.5 and though she has been examined, there is no evidence to say that there was forcible sexual intercourse and apart from that, there are no injuries found on the body including genitalia at the time of examination.
Further, her testimony reveals clothes and materials are taken and sent for FSL.

The FSL report reveals that seminal stains were not detected in item No.1 pubic hair, item No.3 shirt, item No.4 pant swab, item No.5 underwear, NC: 2026:KHC:5764-DB HC-KAR item No.6 pubic hair, item No.7 urethral swab, item No.8 vaginal swab, item No.10 rectal swab, item The State Of Karnataka vs Dinesha @ Dini @ Dayananda on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130155103/
4 No.11 chudidar top, item No.13 chudidar pant, item No.14 brassier and item No.15 petticot and spermatozoa were not detected in item No.9 and the content of item No.2 was disintegrated.

sentences.text: On the basis of the FSL report Ex.P.6, the doctor has given final opinion stating that as per the general physical examination, genital examination and RFSL report, there are no evidence to say that recent sexual intercourse has taken place.

11. The Trial Court has taken note of the material on record, particularly the judgment in the case of NAREDRAKUMAR v. STATE (NCT OF DELHI) reported in 2012 SAR (Crl.) 511 SC, wherein the Apex Court has made an observation that "where evidence of prosecutrix is found suffering from serious infirmities and making deliberate improvements on material point with a view to rule out consent on her part and there being no injuries on her person, no reliance can be placed upon her evidence."

entities.text: NAREDRAKUMAR v. STATE (NCT OF DELHI) reported in 2012 SAR (Crl.) 511 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Trial Court taking note of the same, comes to the conclusion that this judgment is aptly applicable to the case on hand and in detail NC: 2026:KHC:5764-DB HC-KAR discussed in paragraph No.20 that the evidence of P.W.1 is suffering from material contradiction and omissions,
which infirm the case of the prosecution.
Besides, her evidence is not supported by the medical evidence and hence, acquitted the accused.

12. Having taken note of the material available on record, though the learned High Court Government Pleader would submit that the victim girl is aged about 15 years and even though she is a minor as defined under Section 2(d) of POCSO Act, there must be material before the Court with regard to the charges alleged against the accused and there is no any ingredients of the offences,
which have been invoked against the accused.

The evidence of P.W.1 is not consistent and the evidence of P.W.2 and the evidence of the brother of the victim is only based on the say of P.W.1 and P.W.1 evidence is not supported by medical evidence.

The Trial Court in detail taken note of the medical evidence as well as the FSL report and when such material not indicates the act of the accused, we do not find any ground to reverse the finding of the Trial Court.

- 10 - NC: 2026:KHC:5764-DB HC-KAR Point No.(ii):
13.

In view of the discussions made above, we pass the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Appeal is dismissed.
